documents.title: For Students (AI guidance)
documents.stance_why: The page says "Some of your faculty may invite you to use generative AI tools" and others "restrict their use entirely", with a syllabus statement deciding, so the decision is delegated; the "assume that it is forbidden" fallback applies only when a syllabus is silent.
documents.summary: Short student page: students may be invited to use AI or be restricted, depending on each faculty member's syllabus statement. Unspecified use is assumed forbidden, violations can be Honor Code cases, and students stay responsible for accuracy.

units.why: The page says "you have access to several generative AI tools with your Middlebury credentials", so the university provides sanctioned tools; this is a statement of fact to all students (informs, P17).
units.anchor: you have access to several generative AI tools with your Middlebury credentials

units.why: "places an enormous responsibility on you to consider the potential benefits and harms" frames ethical responsibility of the student; closest type is P53 (harms) rather than P29 since no submission is mentioned.
units.anchor: places an enormous responsibility on you to consider the potential benefits and harms

units.why: "Some of your faculty may invite you to use generative AI tools" while others "restrict their use entirely" means the rule varies by instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: some faculty may restrict their use entirely

units.why: "Your faculty should include a syllabus statement indicating what is allowed and what is not allowed" tells instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Your faculty should include a syllabus statement indicating what is allowed

units.why: "failure to comply with class policies prohibiting generative AI use could be construed as an Honor Code violation" classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: could be construed as an Honor Code violation, which could result in disciplinary action

units.why: "you should assume that it is forbidden unless the professor grants you permission verbally or in writing" sets the fallback when a syllabus is silent, so P06 and a restrictive stance.
units.anchor: you should assume that it is forbidden unless the professor grants you permission

units.why: "You are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any work you submit" makes students own submitted work, including AI-assisted work (P29).
units.anchor: You are responsible for the accuracy and integrity of any work you submit

units.why: "We encourage you to participate in events and other learning opportunities" about generative AI is encouragement of AI literacy learning; no type covers student AI-literacy events (P63 is faculty-only).
units.anchor: We encourage you to participate in events and other learning opportunities
units.uncovered_note: Institution encourages students to attend events and learning opportunities to deepen understanding of generative AI.

units.why: "Middlebury is committed to helping our students engage critically with generative AI tools" is an institutional commitment stating purpose and principles (P56).
units.anchor: committed to helping our students engage critically with generative AI tools

documents.title: For Faculty (AI guidance)
documents.stance_why: "Middlebury faculty are empowered to choose their approach" and the page supplies three syllabus options, so it sets no single stance and offers tiers.
documents.summary: Faculty guidance saying instructors choose their own approach, with three sample syllabus statements (prohibited, limited, supported). It also gives cautious advice on AI detectors, recommending dialogue over reliance on detection.

units.why: "Middlebury faculty are empowered to choose their approach" puts the decision with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: faculty are empowered to choose their approach to teaching with generative AI

units.why: "Faculty are asked to provide guidance to students via the course syllabus" asks instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Faculty are asked to provide guidance to students via the course syllabus

units.why: "and to discuss their expectations in class" asks instructors to talk through expectations; P09 (communicating expectations) is the nearest type and P10 does not apply since it concerns students asking.
units.anchor: discuss their expectations in class

units.why: "Middlebury has provided three syllabus statements" (prohibited, limited, allowed/supported) is a set of named options, so P05.
units.anchor: Middlebury has provided three syllabus statements that instructors can use or adapt

units.why: "for each assignment, you can provide guidance on appropriate and inappropriate uses" lets rules vary by assignment (P04), recommending specificity.
units.anchor: for each assignment, you can provide guidance on appropriate and inappropriate uses
units.frag_start: We recommend starting with this language

units.why: Option 1: "Using AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard) is forbidden in this class" bans AI on all work in the course (P01).
units.anchor: Using AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard) is forbidden in this class.

units.why: "Any use of generative AI tools will be treated as a violation of Middlebury's Honor Code" in Option 1 treats AI use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Any use of generative AI tools will be treated as a violation of Middlebury's

units.why: Option 2: "You may use AI tools ... to help generate ideas and brainstorm" permits brainstorming (P15).
units.anchor: You may use AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Bard) to help generate ideas and brainstorm

units.why: "only on assignments for which I have given permission to use AI tools, as specified on the syllabus" makes permission per assignment (P04).
units.anchor: only on assignments for which I have given permission to use AI tools

units.why: "Outputs generated by these programs may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic" warns that AI output can be wrong (P31).
units.anchor: Outputs generated by these programs may be inaccurate, incomplete, or otherwise problematic

units.why: "I will hold you accountable for the accuracy of your work" makes students responsible for verifying AI-assisted work; P31 fits as the point is accuracy, not general ownership.
units.anchor: I will hold you accountable for the accuracy of your work

units.why: "use of AI may also limit your own independent thinking and creativity" warns that AI can undermine thinking, a learning rationale (P41).
units.anchor: use of AI may also limit your own independent thinking and creativity
units.frag_start: Be aware that use of AI

units.why: "Do not submit any work generated by an AI tool as your own" forbids submitting AI-produced work (P19).
units.anchor: Do not submit any work generated by an AI tool as your own.

units.why: "it should be cited like any other reference material (e.g., MLA or APA style citation)" requires citing AI material (P24).
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.why: "Any un-cited or inappropriate use of AI tools will be treated as a violation of Middlebury's Honor Code" makes nondisclosed use misconduct (P36; P28 also fits but the misconduct classification is the point).
units.anchor: Any un-cited or inappropriate use of AI tools will be treated as a violation

units.why: Option 3: "You are expected to use AI tools" makes AI use expected, a default of encouragement (P02).
units.anchor: You are expected to use AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT and image generation tools)

units.why: "some assignments will require it, with appropriate citation" builds AI into assignments (P02, require).
units.anchor: some assignments will require it, with appropriate citation

units.why: "Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and we will be learning that skill together" treats AI use as a professional skill taught in the course (P44).
units.anchor: Learning to use AI is an emerging skill and we will be learning that skill

units.why: "If you have concerns about using these tools, please talk to me ... so that we can find suitable alternatives" provides alternatives to required AI (P51).
units.anchor: please talk to me about your concerns so that we can find suitable alternatives

units.why: "Content detectors such as Turnitin, Pangram, and GPTZero look for repetitive phrasing" describes how detection tools identify AI content (P40, informs).
units.anchor: Content detectors such as Turnitin, Pangram, and GPTZero look for repetitive phrasing

units.why: "AI detectors have varied reliability, can demonstrate bias against non-native English speakers" states detectors are unreliable and biased (P39).
units.anchor: AI detectors have varied reliability, can demonstrate bias against non-native English speakers
units.frag_start: At this time, AI detectors have

units.why: "we recommend that faculty who employ AI detectors do so as supplementary tools ... rather than ... the sole basis" says not to rely on detectors alone as proof (P39).
units.anchor: rather than use these detectors as the sole basis for evaluating academic misconduct

units.why: "pedagogical practices that are resilient to technological disruption because they center what AI cannot replicate" calls for redesigning teaching around AI (P35, informs).
units.anchor: pedagogical practices that are resilient to technological disruption

units.why: "Middlebury is investing in faculty to support the development of new teaching practices" is support for faculty adapting to AI (P63).
units.anchor: Middlebury is investing in faculty to support the development of new teaching practices

units.why: "Stepping up policing around AI use builds an adversarial atmosphere of distrust" argues against policing AI use; P60 (decline to police) is nearest though it is a quoted rationale rather than a staff pledge.
units.anchor: Stepping up policing around AI use builds an adversarial atmosphere of distrust

units.why: "Rather than rely on detection software, MIT suggests that faculty have transparent dialogues about AI use" recommends dialogue and engagement over detectors (P39).
units.anchor: faculty have transparent dialogues about AI use, foster intrinsic motivation

documents.title: AI Policies / principles page
documents.stance_why: The page states principles and points to data classification and IP rules but says "Individual instructors may provide additional guidelines around AI use in their courses", so course stance is delegated.
documents.summary: Principle-level page noting that AI use must follow existing data, IT and IP policies and that the policy will evolve. It leaves course-level rules to instructors.

units.why: "Middlebury College recognizes the profound impact these technologies are having" opens the page with an institutional framing (P56).
units.anchor: Middlebury College recognizes the profound impact these technologies are having

units.why: "guidance and policy will continue to develop along with the capabilities of the technology" says the policy is provisional (P54).
units.anchor: guidance and policy will continue to develop along with the capabilities of the technology

units.why: "AI use at Middlebury must comply with institutional policies" sets the scope that existing policies apply to AI (P56).
units.anchor: AI use at Middlebury must comply with institutional policies
units.frag_start: As with any technology, AI use

units.why: "AI data should be restricted to public data (Level 1)" limits what data enter AI tools (P50).
units.anchor: AI data should be restricted to public data (Level 1)

units.why: "please request a consultation with ITS" is the route for using non-public data with a specific AI tool (P50).
units.anchor: please request a consultation with ITS

units.why: "carefully review the AI tool's terms of service for any intellectual property or copyright clauses" concerns licensing and ownership (P52).
units.anchor: carefully review the AI tool's terms of service for any intellectual property

units.why: "Community members are expected to avoid actions that could compromise the functionality of IT resources or the privacy of others" is the IT responsible-use rule applied to AI (P50).
units.anchor: expected to avoid actions that could compromise the functionality of IT resources

units.why: "Before using an AI technology make sure you understand how it will treat the content you enter" ties AI use to IP and data handling (P52; P50 less apt since privacy is not named).
units.anchor: Before using an AI technology make sure you understand how it will treat the content

units.why: "Individual instructors may provide additional guidelines around AI use in their courses" leaves further rules to instructors (P04); it appears twice, coded once.
units.anchor: Individual instructors may provide additional guidelines around AI use in their courses.

units.why: "Protect academic standards and rigor, support authentic student learning" states the goal of the academic integrity policy (P56).
units.anchor: Protect academic standards and rigor, support authentic student learning

notes: Coder A. Only the three included university-layer documents coded. Duplicate sentence "Individual instructors may provide additional guidelines" coded once. One UNCOVERED unit (student encouragement to attend AI learning events).
